narrative.overview:
The user selected a flight-operations dashboard and then asked for a more ambitious animated frontend. The graphite, mint, and blue identity remains; larger typography and detailed schematic spacecraft give the relative flight scene more presence. Configuration, capture, and guidance stay readable beside the scene so researchers can compare commands with measured effects.

Motion follows backend measurements. A separate, labelled illustrative Earth and static star field frame the spacecraft. Controls remain stable, native, and task-focused; the only authored confirmation animation follows a server-verified capture.
keyCharacteristics: Measured motion with a labelled illustrative backdrop
dos: Do show units beside every configurable quantity and measurement.
Do keep numerical telemetry tied to backend events.
Do label the deterministic planner and provider fallback honestly.
Do preserve standard form semantics and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep schematic models and illustrative scenery explicitly labelled.
Do reserve capture confirmation for the server's terminal docked event.
donts: Don't use animation to conceal latency or invent a physical outcome.
Don't turn an observed success rate into an unqualified accuracy guarantee.
